proof.criterion: Round 3's first failure: A1's write row. The row passes with no retries, the write's variance is named from measurement, and the 1 s bound is untouched.

proof.command: source /legion/harness/env.sh && cd packages/dispatch && bun e2e/run.ts -- bunx playwright test --config e2e/playwright.config.ts heavy-bodies.e2e.ts --project=chromium -g 'a document write of each heavy body' --retries=0, twenty times; and a throwaway Go rig driving 20 writes with phase timers, GODEBUG=gctrace=1 and allocation per write window.
proof.observed: The row passes 20 of 20 with --retries=0 (and three more runs of my own since). The variance is the settlement each write queues landing on the writes after it, not the write's own work: writes 1-5 of every run allocate 176.2 MB and take 474-592 ms, and from write 6 - the first to run beside a settlement, the window being 2 s and the writes ~550 ms apart - the window's allocation climbs to 200-520 MB and the time to 594-1,186 ms. The control is flat: the same 20 writes with a 4 s gap allocate 165.8-176.2 MB throughout and 19 of 20 are under 800 ms. Two cuts landed - AppendUpdateTx reads the update's item count from its own header instead of decoding it into a throwaway document, and LoadDoc validates the stored history by the same header check instead of a full decode ygo repeats a step later - worth 153 ms of CPU and 72 MB of allocation a write.
proof.negativeControl: The 4 s-gap control is the measurement that names the cause rather than describing the symptom: same code, same body, same pod, and the tail disappears when no settlement runs beside a write. A second factor was measured and reported rather than claimed as the cause: giving each document its own issue (so the upload and the settlement do not contend on one issue row's lock) cut the over-800 count from 4-6 to 2 per run but left the spikes.

trickyParts: The nesting bound cannot be expressed with micromark's `disable` (a disabled construct name is refused for every attempt, including list's attempts on itself), so block-nesting.ts wraps the `list` and `blockQuote` objects micromark-core-commonmark exports, in place, once, idempotently, from lib-remark-directive-plugin.ts's module scope. A second copy of micromark-core-commonmark in the tree would escape the wrap, which is why a proof-editor row asserts the bound through a bare unified().use(remarkParse) processor.

The worker cannot rebuild a document with Schema.nodeFromJSON: milkdown's parser writes title: null for a picture with no title, where the schema declares a string, so every body holding a picture was refused on rebuild. markdown-engine.ts's own documentFromJSON is the path, and a unit row guards it.

The harness's Playwright trace recorder (trace: retain-on-failure) snapshots the DOM on every mutation, so an earlier painter that appended into the live element measured 13.7-61 s with the main thread apparently idle. Three independent clocks stopping together is what identified it. The painter now builds off the page and attaches in batches of 500 nodes, which is fast with the recorder on.

content-visibility: auto helps Chromium and actively hurts WebKit once the attach is batched (longest gap 4,766 ms with the rule, 141 ms without), because a per-element layout read then forces items relevant one at a time. The rule is deleted and the batching carries it in every engine.

The Go package internal/dispatch/pmdoc needs an explicit -timeout in an issue pod: with this branch's rows skipped it already takes 731 s, past go test's 600 s default, and the panic names main's own TestUpdateIsLinearInTheBlockCount. Use go test -p 1 -timeout 40m.

A bullet list of n items is n+1 blocks, not 2n+1: the list and each item's paragraph, since a list item is not a block. The deferral's threshold arithmetic rests on that (43-48 microseconds a block, measured either side of the bound).
deviations: The three plan departures the architect accepted on 2026-10-29 at 09:44Z, with its four conditions, all met: the text shows at once and stays selectable (browser row); a worker that cannot start, cannot load its chunk, crashes or misses its deadline falls back to parsing on the page rather than to no formatting (browser row plus three unit rows), so data-markdown-fallback keeps meaning only that the parser refused the body; the late paint keeps the reader's place (two rows, Chromium and WebKit); and the editor's measured ~1.4 s is recorded in the PR's Not proven / risk and in a changelog fragment.

Scope the architect approved during the round: a document of more than 2,000 blocks leaves its block index to the settlement already in the tree. A caller sees the same 201, artifact, version and documentBlocks advice, but until the settlement indexes them a reference into such a document resolves to no block and a backlink names the document rather than the block holding the mention.

The write now reads its markdown once instead of five times (the architect had asked only for a batched index; the index was already one statement per table, which CopyFrom would improve by 30-50 ms at the cost of the on-conflict-do-update that makes a re-index idempotent, so that was rejected and this was done instead).

The document-write row holds the one parse-bound body ('- ' x 49 padded with blank lines to the cap) to its steady state: the row writes it once to warm the process, records that first write's time as an annotation, and asserts the second under 1,000 ms. The architect directed this after the measurement. The cost is goldmark's own blankLines slice, which grows with depth times lines (~3.1 M entries, ~75 MB at the cap); the goldmark change that would fix it is ruled out.

The simplify pass applied 14 findings and skipped 2 (a per-parse registry in block-nesting.ts, which the reviewer itself rated 0.55; and the deliberately independent constants in the proof-editor test, which restate the Go bound on purpose). Two of the applied findings were regressions this change had introduced: a forced layout on every paint, and a per-exit re-slice in the directive-container split.

Round 2 of review: the architect ruled a quarter-size baseline at 2.5x for the write row's linearity assertion, then accepted the correction - a quarter is two doublings, so a linear write reads about 4x (measured 4.25x and 4.69x) and 2.5x would have asserted the write is sublinear. Shipped: a half-size body of the same shape, the full body timed first (whichever size is written first pays ~200 ms of shape warm-up, and body-first keeps the absolute bound measuring what it has always measured), 3.5x, on the three parse-dominated rows, with the 1,000 ms bound unconditional on all eight.

The suite gained a browser row for the fresh-mount streaming defect, on the tester's recipe and at its suggestion: the defect reached review twice and no existing row drove a reader opening the live view mid-stream. It carries two vacuity guards (a part-built body and a frame's text must each have been recorded), because the same shape at 900 paragraphs and 150 ms frames is green against the defective code.
openQuestions: The write row's 1,000 ms absolute assertion reds about 1 in 5 runs on a two-core Broadwell pod for main@origin as well as for this head; CI's runners are where the architect judges it, and the tester judges linearity on the pod. If CI's own runners turn out to be that slow, the bound is the architect's to revisit with the head-against-base table in the body.
discoveredComplexity: WebKit spends 2.2-2.8 s inserting and laying out 8,000 list items where Chromium and Firefox spend 260-455 ms, so the single attach had to become batched; after it, WebKit is the fastest of the three on those rows (107-185 ms).

A hover card over a long body closed in WebKit and Firefox before its preview formatted, because the late paint's own scroll fired the close path, and then a synthetic pointermove at the unchanged pointer position fired it again. The reader never saw the formatted preview in those engines. Both are fixed in RefPreview.tsx and proven by the row in all three engines.

The reader's-place row's 1-in-10 WebKit failure was not the late paint: the deep link marks the conversation read, every card loses its 24 px unread pill, the page loses 312 px and WebKit's scroll anchoring absorbs it. The failing run's own log shows the late paint moved the content 0 px. The row now takes its first measurement once the page has held it for 600 ms.

goldmark's blank-line bookkeeping is superlinear in depth times lines for a body that holds blocks open across thousands of blank lines. It is the one shape of this issue's family left unfixed, and it is in the vendored parser.
